capabilities: Rename the note's file to match its first H1 heading
Strip markdown formatting and replace illegal filename characters with dashes
Truncate filenames to 200 characters for cross-platform compatibility
Run the sync from the command palette or a user-assigned hotkey
Show a notification on sync success or failure
disambiguation: Not a cross-device sync tool; 'sync' here means renaming the file to match the note's H1 heading on demand.
extras: At the time of writing the plugin is not yet in the community plugin directory and must be installed manually; the README recommends disabling Obsidian's 'Show inline title' setting to avoid showing the title twice.
intentEvidence: This plugin is inspired by obsidian-filename-heading-sync but takes a different approach
problem: Obsidian doesn't provide a one-command way to make a note's filename follow its H1 heading, and automatic heading-sync plugins don't suit users who want explicit control over renames.

relations.evidence: This plugin is inspired by obsidian-filename-heading-sync but takes a different approach

summary: Manual-command plugin that renames a note's file to match its first H1 heading, sanitizing the title into a valid filename.
